question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

It is 2036. Looking back, 5 landmark papers each settled this question in a way that surprised the field, because of how they approached it. For each paper, describe what it measured, analyzed, or did, as a concrete idea a research lab could pursue today. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after a priming stimulus
ideas.description: Prime cells (e.g., fibroblasts, macrophages, or neurons) with a stimulus, then use degron tags (dTAG/AID) to rapidly deplete FOS/JUN family members after priming but before restimulation. If the enhanced secondary response and chromatin accessibility persist without AP-1, AP-1 is only an initiator. If they vanish, AP-1 actively maintains the memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracing of memory inheritance
ideas.description: Combine barcoded lineage tracing with paired scATAC/scRNA and live AP-1 reporters. Compare sister cells across several divisions after transient stimulation, and test whether AP-1 motif accessibility and response magnitude are inherited more strongly than expected from shared lineage or noise.

ideas.title: Optogenetic AP-1 pulses with decay-kinetics mapping
ideas.description: Deliver defined optogenetic or chemogenetic pulses of AP-1 activity that vary in dose, duration, and spacing. Then measure how long enhancer accessibility, H3K27ac, and transcriptional hyperresponsiveness last. The result is a quantitative memory curve that shows whether AP-1 activity alone is sufficient to write memory and how its persistence compares with that of other transcription factors.

ideas.title: Locus-specific AP-1 site editing and dCas9 recruitment
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing to mutate individual AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers. Separately, use dCas9-based recruitment of AP-1 or of chromatin remodelers (SWI/SNF, BAF) to naive loci. Together these test whether AP-1 binding at a specific site is necessary and sufficient for maintained accessibility and faster reactivation, independent of global AP-1 changes.

ideas.title: In vivo cross-context memory comparison with live-binding imaging
ideas.description: Run parallel experiments in mouse tissue (e.g., skin inflammatory memory, neuronal activity, or trained immunity) with AP-1 knockouts. Pair the knockouts with single-molecule tracking of AP-1 residence time and CUT&Tag over weeks. The goal is to determine whether AP-1 stays bound to enhancers, only leaves behind a pioneer-opened chromatin state, or is replaced by other factors, and whether this holds across tissues.
